defs.def: a word or words that a particular person, animal, place or thing is known by 名字；名称

ex.s: I considered this when I met a thoughtful young businessman named Anthony.
ex.t: 当我遇到一位名叫安东尼、深思熟虑的年轻商人时，我想到了这一点。

ex.s: As you listen, make notes of key information such as names, numbers, facts and instructions.
ex.t: 听的时候，把关键信息记下来，比如姓名、数字、事实和指示。

ex.s: “What is your name? ” is a question most frequently asked when people meet for the first time.
ex.t: “你叫什么名字？”是人们初次见面时最常问的问题。

ex.s: I really envy youD. that name rings a bell
ex.t: 我真羡慕你。D. 那个名字听起来很耳熟。

ex.s: In a class discussion, I was invited to explain the meaning of my name.
ex.t: 在一次课堂讨论中，我被邀请解释我名字的含义。

ex.s: Many works of fiction appeared without the names of the authors, often with something like “By a lady.”Novels, for the most part, were looked upon as silly, immoral, or just plain bad.
ex.t: 许多小说作品出版时没有作者名字，往往只署类似“一位女士著”。小说在很大程度上被看作愚蠢、不道德，或者干脆就是烂。

ex.s: Does the name of the college you attend really matter？Research on the question   7  （suggest）that，for most students，it doesn't.
ex.t: 你所上的大学的名字真的重要吗？对这个问题的研究   7  （suggest）表明，对大多数学生来说，并不重要。

ex.s: His effort to reunite families with lost medals began with a Christmas gift from his mother, a Purple Heart with the name Corrado A.
ex.t: 他让家庭与丢失勋章重聚的努力，始于母亲送的一份圣诞礼物——一枚刻着科拉多·A之名的紫心勋章。

ex.s: My name is Alice.
ex.t: 我的名字叫Alice。

ex.s: My friends checked and came back shouting, “Amy, you got the main role! ” Sure enough, my name was at the top.
ex.t: 我的朋友们查看后跑回来喊道："艾米，你拿到主角了！"果然，我的名字在最上面。

ex.s: After that incident, I stopped acting as a “Chinese teacher.” Instead of correcting others when they were struggling to pronounce my name, I just smiled and nodded approvingly.
ex.t: 那次事件后，我不再担任“汉语老师”。“当别人挣扎着说出我的名字时，我没有纠正别人，我只是微笑着点头表示赞许。

ex.s: He posted his   49  on a social networking website, and received thousands of e-mails, including thirty from actual Elizabeth Gallagbers with the   50  passports, “More   51  , there are hundreds of Canadians who are interested in   52   their name to Elizabeth Gallagher,” Axani said.
ex.t: 他在一家社交网站上发布了他的____，收到了数千封电子邮件，其中包括三十封来自真正的伊丽莎白·加拉赫的邮件，她们持有____护照。“更有____，有数百名加拿大人有兴趣把他们的名字改成伊丽莎白·加拉赫，”阿克萨尼说。

ex.s: Every time I gave a self-introduction, I had to explain how to pronounce my name at least five times, yet they still could not say it the way I did.
ex.t: 每次我作自我介绍时，都不得不把我的名字怎么读解释至少五遍，可他们还是说不出我那种读法。

defs.def: a reputation that sb/sth has; the opinion that people have about sb/sth 名誉；名声；名气

ex.s: You must be named Elizabeth Gallahgher and have a Candian 42     .
ex.t: 你必须名叫伊丽莎白·加拉赫，并且持有一本加拿大护照。

ex.s: There' s nothing very complicated about this usage, a budget line is one of the lines in the budget, with the service or good to be purchased named and the cost quantified,
ex.t: 这种用法并不复杂，预算线就是预算中的一条线，注明要购买的服务或商品并量化成本，

ex.s: When I was 17， I read a magazine article about a museum called the McNay， once the home of a watercolorist named Marian McNay． She had requested the community to turn it into a museum upon her death． On a sunny Saturday， Sally and I drove over to the museum． She asked， "Do you have the address？ ""No， but I'll recognize it， there was a picture in the magazine．
ex.t: 我17岁时，读到一篇杂志文章，介绍一家叫麦克奈的博物馆，它曾是水彩画家玛丽安·麦克奈的故居。她曾要求社区在她去世后将其改为博物馆。一个阳光明媚的周六，萨莉和我开车去了博物馆。她问："你有地址吗？""没有，但我会认出来的，杂志上有照片。"

ex.s: care only about the names of birds
ex.t: 只关心鸟的名字

defs.def: having a name or a reputation of the kind mentioned, especially one that is known by a lot of people 构成复合形容词

ex.s: They looked a bit like eggs, which led to the name “eggplant”.
ex.t: 它们看起来有点像蛋，因此得名“茄子”。

ex.s: William Sydney Porter (1862-1910), whose pen name was O.
ex.t: 威廉\u00b7悉尼\u00b7波特（1862-1910），笔名欧\u00b7亨利。

ex.s: The little boy -his name was Bernard-had interested her very much.
ex.t: 他很想赚些钱，但我看不出他能做什么。"

ex.s: My name is Mireya Mayor.
ex.t: 我叫米雷娅·马约尔。

ex.s: “What’s his name?” I asked the instructor.
ex.t: "他叫什么名字？"我问教练。

defs.def: for sb; showing that sth officially belongs to sb 为（某人）；在 … 名下

ex.s: John Lennon and Paul McCartney were named composers of the year.
ex.t: 约翰·列农和保罗·麦卡特尼被评为年度作曲家。

ex.s: The vehicle — named the Transition – has two seats, four wheels and wings that fold up so it can be driven like a car.
ex.t: 这辆名为Transition的车有两个座位、四个轮子和可折叠的机翼，因此可以像汽车一样驾驶。

ex.s: I live in the city now, and my paperboy is a lady named Edna with three kids.
ex.t: 我现在住在城里，我的送报员是一位叫埃德娜的女士，她有三个孩子。

ex.s: The Intelligent Transport team at Newcastle University have turned an electric car into a mobile laboratory named “Drive LAB” in order to understand the challenges faced by older drivers and to discover where the key stress points are.
ex.t: 纽卡斯尔大学的智能交通团队把一辆电动汽车改造成了一个名为“Drive LAB”的移动实验室，以了解老年驾驶者面临的挑战，并找出关键的压力点在哪里。

ex.s: Scene 1: Bob dining with Jimmy at “Big Joe” Brady’s twenty years ago Scene 2: Bob making his fortune in the West Scene 3: Bob and Jimmy meeting again after twenty years The story is about two friends named Bob and Jimmy.
ex.t: 场景1：二十年前鲍勃和吉米在＂大乔＂布雷迪餐厅吃饭 场景2：鲍勃在西部发家致富 场景3：二十年后鲍勃和吉米重逢 故事是关于叫鲍勃和吉米的两个朋友。

ex.s: Housewarming parties get their name from the fact that a long time ago people would actually bring firewood to a new home as a gift.
ex.t: 暖房派对得名于这样一个事实：很久以前，人们会真的带木柴作为礼物送进新家。

ex.s: Head Chef David Thompson, who received a Michelin star for his Loodon-based Thai restaurant of the same name, opened this branch in the Metropolitan Hotel in 2010.
ex.t: 主厨大卫·汤普森曾凭借其位于伦敦的同名泰国餐厅获得米其林一星，他于2010年在大都会酒店开设了这家分店。

ex.s: ■On the same sheet of paper, write or type your name, address, telephone number, and birth date.
ex.t: ■在同一张纸上，手写或打印你的姓名、地址、电话号码和出生日期。

defs.def: using the authority of sb/sth; as a representative of sb/sth 凭 … 的权威；代表
以 … 的名义；以 … 为借口
a person or thing that is well known and respected in a particular field 大名鼎鼎的人；重量级人物；影响巨大的事物

ex.s: A British woman who won a S1 million prize after she was named the World's Best Teacher will use the cash to bring inspirational figures into UK schools.
ex.t: 一名英国女性在被评上世界最佳教师后赢得了100万美元奖金，她将用这笔钱把励志人物带进英国学校。

ex.s: This beautiful structure, named Glasshouse, is at the centre of a new garden that shows how the Silk Road influences English gardens even in modern times.
ex.t: 这座名为Glasshouse的美丽建筑位于一座新花园的中心，展示了丝绸之路如何在现代仍影响着英国花园。

ex.s: Like Galileo, all the great names in history were curious and asked in discontent, "Why?
ex.t: 像伽利略一样，历史上所有伟大的人物都充满好奇心，不满地问“为什么？”

defs.def: 难记的名字；拗口的名字

ex.s: How did the author feel upon seeing the email sender’s name?
ex.t: 看到邮件发件人的名字时，作者是什么感受？

ex.s: This means. for example，that a scammer could call you from what looks to be a familiar number and talk to you using a voice that sounds exactly like your bank teller 's，ricking you into "confirming " your address，mother's name，and card number.
ex.t: 这意味着，比如说，一个骗子可以给你打电话 从一个看起来熟悉的号码 并用一个声音和你说话 听起来就像你的银行出纳的，让你"确认"你的地址，母亲的名字，和卡片号码。

ex.s: After finishing an order, she calls out the name on the cup.
ex.t: 完成一单后，她会喊出杯子上写的名字。

ex.s: Once in a lecture, the professor tried repeating my name after me over and over in front of thirty classmates.
ex.t: 有一次在课上，教授当着三十名同学的面，一遍又一遍地跟着我重复我的名字。

ex.s: For instance, if an object’s name was meant to sound genderless, like Miuu, participants would still assign a gender to it — they would assume Miuu was a “he” or “she.”
ex.t: 例如，如果一个物体的名字本意是无性别的，比如Miuu，参与者仍会给它赋予性别——他们会假定Miuu是“他”或“她”。

ex.s: She   48   for the woman’s name and address so that she could   49   her.
ex.t: 她____48____那位女士的名字和地址，以便能____49____她。

ex.s: My heart raced when I saw the email sender’s name.
ex.t: 当我看到邮件发件人的名字时，我的心跳加速了。

ex.s: Miss Zhao told us the names of the insects or described their living habits.
ex.t: 赵老师告诉我们昆虫的名字，或描述它们的生活习性。

ex.s: The little boy — his name was Bernard—had interested her very much.
ex.t: 这个小男孩——他的名字叫Bernard——引起了她很大的兴趣。

ex.s: Yet, when something new turns up, more often than not, we do not even know its name.
ex.t: 然而，当新事物出现时，我们往往甚至不知道它的名字。

defs.def: to give a name to sb/sth 命名；给 … 取名

ex.s: Some 60,000 novels were published during the Victorian age, from 1837 to1901; today a casual reader might be able to name a half-dozen of them.
ex.t: 在维多利亚时代，从1837年到1901年，出版了约6万本小说；今天，一个随便的读者也许可以将其中的六分之一命名。

ex.s: Naming them is a challenging task.
ex.t: 给它们命名是一项具有挑战性的任务。

ex.s: Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them.
ex.t: 为每种自然体验命名创造出一种可用的语言，帮助人们认识并参与那些对他们来说最令人满足、最有意义的活动。

ex.s: “Ecological design” is the name John gives to what he does.
ex.t: "生态设计"是约翰对他所做工作的命名。

defs.def: to say the name of sb/sth 说出 … 的名称；叫出 … 的名字

ex.s: It is hard to name a comedy star who hasn’t been on the stage here.
ex.t: 很难说出哪位喜剧明星没有在这个舞台上演出过。

ex.s: He called them by name and asked  19  about their families.
ex.t: 他叫着他们的名字，并询问____19____他们的家人。

ex.s: On a regular day， students at the school sometimes come up to him to say they're not feeling well or other times to tell him about something that happened at break． He knows most of the kids at the school， but can't name each one． Some of them make him know them． Like Faith， who often forgets her backpack in the cafeteria， and Lucy， who just wants a hug．
ex.t: 平常的一天，学校里的学生有时会走到他面前说他们不舒服，有时则会告诉他课间发生的事。他认识学校里大多数孩子，却叫不出每个人的名字。有些孩子让他记住了自己，比如常常把背包忘在食堂的Faith，还有只想拥抱一下的Lucy。

ex.s: I tried to turn on my brain but the engine just wouldn't start.” I should say my name, of course.
ex.t: “我试图启动我的大脑，可引擎就是打不着火。”当然，我应该说我的名字。

ex.s: In front of me was an array of foods I couldn’t even name in my native language.
ex.t: 摆在我面前的是一系列我用母语都叫不出名字的食物。

to choose sb for a job or position 任命；委任
